summary: Tested the readable Core Blue CSS rule (A) and the email palette remap (B). (B) Backend: /api/health is OK. The rendered _reminder_html, wrap_branded and wrapped reminder contain none of the 8 banned colours, and every hex in them is in the guide or status set. A static scan of the email HTML strings found no banned colours. Leftovers: 3 emails still use Core Blue #19CDFF link text on white (details below). (A) Frontend: a new computed-style audit (/app/tests/core_blue_audit.js) ran on /, /pulse, /login, /?portal=modservice, /master-admin, /dashboard, /service-desk, /crm and /staff-portal, light and dark, at 1920 and 390 width, as admin@pulsefitness.com and owner@isodemo.com. Text using the covered utilities (text-[var(--color-brand-cyan)], text-[var(--pulse-primary)], text-[#19CDFF], inline rgb colour) correctly renders rgb(0,145,202) on light surfaces: 47 elements on the landing page and 9 on the MOD login, including the 'Three Services.' headline. Things that correctly stay bright rgb(25,205,255): the landing hero 'Maintain' word, the black navbars, the Service Desk Team Performance dark card, and the MOD footer. Only one element got the darker blue on a dark surface (the landing 95.5% stat card, ratio 4.8, still readable). Nothing became unreadable. Dark theme: dashboard, CRM, staff portal and MOD login are unchanged, with 0 dark-blue elements. Main gaps: two common Core Blue patterns are not covered by the rule, so a lot of bright Core Blue text is still on white in light mode.

ui_bugs.issue: The utility text-[var(--gx-brand-from)] (= #19CDFF) is not in the rule, so the active nav label stays bright #19CDFF on white (1.87:1) in light mode.

ui_bugs.issue: These use inline style={{color:'var(--color-brand-cyan)'}}. The rule only matches inline 'color: rgb(25, 205, 255)', so they stay bright on #F0F0F0 and white (1.64 to 1.87:1).
A white card with data-theme=light sits inside the hero's data-theme=dark wrapper. The nested [data-theme=dark] exclusion wins, so 'Live' and '+£3.1k' stay bright on white (1.87:1).

The card background class bg-[var(--pulse-black,#1B1C1D)] is not in the dark-container exclusions. '95.5%' renders #0091CA on #1B1C1D (4.8:1, readable but dim and not to the guide). It also happens with the theme set to dark, because the landing page has nested light wrappers.

issues: The desk sidebar stays white, and the active 'Dashboard' label is #19CDFF on white (1.87:1). The light-only rule does not cover this. It was like this before.
Many emails use white text on #19CDFF buttons (about 1.9:1), e.g. password reset and welcome. Consider #00121A/#1B1C1D text, as the vehicle-check reminder already does.

action_items: Add text-[var(--gx-brand-from)] to the readable-blue rule in index.css, or swap the active-nav class to a covered one.
Cover inline style 'color: var(--color-brand-cyan)'. Add [style*="color: var(--color-brand-cyan)"] selectors with the same exclusions, or convert those 179 inline styles to the className.
Add bg-[var(--pulse-black,#1B1C1D)] (and similar var-fallback dark bg classes) to the dark-container exclusion list.
Fix the landing hero preview: let a nested [data-theme=light] inside [data-theme=dark] re-enable the rule, or add an explicit class.
Change the email link colour #19CDFF to #0091CA in pulse_upgrade.py:64, mod_bulk_import.py:488 and mod_portal.py:3147. Replace #cfe0ff in the onboarding invite email.
critical_code_review_comments: The index.css rule repeats a roughly 40-item :not(:where(...)) list 20 times. Put the dark-surface ancestors behind one marker class, or use :is() for the utilities, to reduce duplication and the risk of missed entries.
The inline-style matcher depends on React serialising the colour as 'color: rgb(25, 205, 255)'. It misses var() values and any style where colour is not first or after '; '.

The exclusions only look at ancestor classes. Dark surfaces set by inline style or gradients (e.g. style={{background:'#1B1C1D'}}) are not excluded. None were found on the audited pages, but the risk remains elsewhere.
